text:
alex: Heads-up: seeing intermittent packet loss between pods on node pools running GPU workloads in us-west-2. Symptoms start ~10:20 UTC, training jobs report stalled steps and TCP retransmits. Not constant — spikes for ~30s every few minutes.

sam: saw similar on one cluster earlier, thought it was high RDMA traffic. Any pattern by AZ or kernel?

alex: only on geneve-encap overlay (we use Geneve for host-to-host). Native host interfaces fine. Loss visible in application metrics as ~0.15-0.4% p50->p90 spike.

jyoti: can you paste tcpdump from a node during an event? Also want ethtool -k and offload settings.

alex: attaching quick captures and commands I ran:

```
# on host where pod-to-pod loss observed
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -nn udp and dst port 6081 -c 200 -w /tmp/geneve-sample.pcap
sudo ethtool -k ens3
ss -s | grep retrans
kubectl exec -n trainer pod/train-xyz -- curl -sS -D - http://10.42.5.12:8080/health
```

tcpdump snippet (not full pcap):
```
16:20:21.123456 IP 10.0.1.5.57920 > 10.0.2.12.40322: UDP, length 358
16:20:21.123489 IP 10.0.1.5.57920 > 10.0.2.12.40322: UDP, length 1420
16:20:21.153501 IP 10.0.1.5.57920 > 10.0.2.12.40322: UDP, length 1420
# gaps ~30ms then bursts
```

sam: hmm those 1420s indicate fragmentation under MTU 1500? Our Geneve header + outer UDP + ip reduce effective payload. Are these nodes on different ENI types?

alex: both on p4d fleet with mtu set to 9001 on host, but I noticed kube-bridge interfaces (cni) show MTU 1450. Not sure when that changed.

maria: recent kube-proxy / CNI upgrade last week changed default encapsulation settings, maybe a regression in host MTU normalization. I flagged it in the upgrade PR but didn't have repro.

jyoti: let's check offloads — GSO/LRO/GRO interactions with geneve can cause packets to be coalesced and then get dropped when outer headers are constructed. If kernel sends large GSO segments that exceed outer MTU, hardware or NIC driver might drop them intermittently.

sam: agree. Steps to reproduce: enable packet capture on both ends, disable GSO/GRO temporarily:
```
sudo ethtool -K ens3 gso off gro off gso_robust_offload off
# also on tunnel device: ip link set geneve0 mtu 1450
```

alex: did that on a test node, short run looks clean — application retransmits went away for the window where offloads were off.

infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed a canary rollback in cluster-usw2-gpu-3 at 16:05 UTC due to health probes failing (related events: CNI upgrade 2026-02-02T15:48).

maria: if toggling offloads helps, we need to decide whether to adjust MTU on tunnel devices or disable specific offloads in the NIC driver as a stable fix. Disabling GSO cluster-wide could hurt throughput for large message workloads.

jyoti: alternative: enable outer-fragmentation support — kernel 5.15+ has geneve GSO fixes, but driver + NIC firmware matters. Check kernel version and current tx/rx descriptor configs.

alex: nodes are on kernel 5.10.70. That could be the problem — geneve gso bugfix landed in later kernels.

sam: options: 1) upgrade kernel across GPU fleet (big ops), 2) adjust MTU on pod/tunnel interfaces to avoid GSO creation, 3) toggle offloads per-node as a targeted workaround, 4) pin CNI to previous working version.

maria: immediate mitigation: roll a daemonset that sets geneve MTU to 1400 and disables GSO only on nodes with problematic NIC driver (target by instance-type label). Can we get metrics to see which instance-types saw the spikes?

alex: I pushed a quick Fluentbit rule to tag logs by instance-type and added metric filters in prometheus for tcp_retransmits per-node. Early charts show p4d.24xlarge nodes highest.

jyoti: file a runbook entry. I'll draft kernel-upgrade plan but prefer smaller step first: daemonset with ip link and ethtool toggles + CI to validate throughput. We'll need perf test to ensure no unacceptable latency regressions.

sam: I can prepare a canary: apply to one AZ, monitor training steps and network retransmits for 30m. If stable, expand.

alex: launched canary patch at 16:35 UTC (geneve mtu 1400 + disable gso on ens3). Initial 40m look: retransmits fell ~90% on canary nodes, application errors gone.

maria: good. Next: schedule kernel upgrade for next maintenance window and talk to cloud provider about NIC firmware/driver updates. Also open a CNI bug with the team that shipped the change.

jyoti: created infra ticket INF-4721 with details, logs, pcap and suggested remediation. Linking here: https://redwood.internal/infra/INF-4721

alex: thanks all. Will keep thread updated if we see regression after expanding canary. :thumbsup:

sam: one more note — if anyone sees sudden spikes after re-enabling offloads, collect /proc/net/softnet_stat and dmesg; driver drops often report skb irregularities.

maria: noted. Closing loop once kernel plan approved.

alex: marking nodes patched and monitoring.
